package: K01-T3 HTTP playback planning and attempt-scoped HLS routing

regression.initial_observation: After successful FFmpeg encoding and activation, owner GET /api/media-source returned an ERROR playback plan.
regression.cause: Playback URL parsing and the HLS edge worker mapped only legacy videos/<id>/v/<version> keys; the encoder now stores videos/<id>/v/<version>/attempts/<attemptId>.
regression.fix: The signed delivery version is now <version>~<attemptId>; the app signs the complete value and the edge Worker maps it to the exact attempt prefix. Legacy version URLs keep their existing mapping.

postgres_http_worker_test.http: real Next dev server on loopback; guest Studio pipeline 401; owner pipeline 200 with SUCCEEDED/DONE and active asset; guest playback plan 403 without URL; owner /api/media-source READY with SELF_HLS URL

result.eslint: PASS, zero errors; one import/no-anonymous-default-export warning remains in the existing edge Worker export

assertions: The signed playback URL for an attempt asset includes the exact attempt UUID and verifies against the edge token contract.
The edge Worker fetches the master playlist from videos/<videoId>/v/<version>/attempts/<attemptId>/master.m3u8, not the legacy prefix.
The player preserves attempt identity when replacing a token and refuses to rewrite a URL for a different attempt.
The Studio API omits bucket and object-key storage details.
limitations: The test exercises playback planning over HTTP, not actual HLS segment delivery through a deployed Cloudflare Worker.
The S3-shaped object store is a loopback fixture, not Cloudflare R2; provider semantics and edge cache/CORS are unverified.
Studio upload HTTP, browser playback, deployed Worker-first rollout and independent review remain open; K01-T3/K35 are partial.
